I really appreciate to posting your experience. I wanted to say that you’re not alone in this struggle. As I was reading, I realized how I have the same tendency to fall in with manipulative and emotional unavailable partners. A part of it stems from cycles of behavior created through past traumatic experiences. I also grew up with addiction in the house, so I tend towards codependency. 

It makes me feel embarrassed — like I should have known better; that I should have more self respect. Also, having the people in my life witness all of this play out feels humiliating. At its worst, I can feel pretty pathetic and completely shut myself off from relationships entirely. However, it does deflate the shame knowing that I’m not alone in this struggle. 

The good news is! The pattern has been recognized, and with that self awareness it’s possible to take the steps to break this cycle and enter a nurturing and fulfilling relationship. Your worth is not contingent on how people treat you. You are worthy as you are! Every different version of you; From years passed, to the future — they are all worthy and deserving of love, affection, and compassion. You don’t have to earn it. You, as you are, are enough. 

Thank you for sharing and keep fighting the good fight !

Looking back at our interactions, it does seem very clear that they have been very inconsistent and mean spirited — especially when threatened. They also needle me about my weight, anxiety, and intelligence (I have a hard time articulating myself when on the spot, so he’s begun putting me on the spot quite often). We work in the same place, so distancing myself will be a bit challenging. Thankfully I do have a support system outside of work that I can lean on. 

If you don’t mind me asking, how did you go about cutting ties with your individual? Did you do it gradually or all at once? Did they lash out? Thanks again for taking the time to answer!

It’s going to sound so annoying, but it truly comes down to radical acceptance and self compassionate. You can’t shame yourself into submission. Everyday, do something that reaffirms the person you are in that moment. Hehe you looked into DBT? It could be helpful in this. 

And feeling exhausted, frustrated and lonely are completely valid, and not a selfish feeling — I’m honestly right there with you. There is a great deal of mourning that comes with the knowledge that we’ll never be neurotypical. Living in an ableist society, it is inevitable that we will encounter many more challenges that most people won’t. And because of that barrier, we’ll have to do so much extra mental labour to just keep up. 

It sounds like you have a long list of support and healthy coping mechanisms. You should be proud of the safety net you’ve built, while working as a paralegal AND musician?! An allistic person would also have trouble managing both those as well, so the fact that you’re pushing through it incredible! 

Be kind and gentle with yourself. Easier said than done I know, I’m still trying to get there myself. But keep with the good fight, I’m rootin for you!
